sections.html:
Walton County owners deal with two offices. The tax collector bills and collects. The property appraiser sets values and exemptions. The collector runs three branches: the DeFuniak Springs courthouse for north Walton, the Santa Rosa Beach courthouse annex for south Walton, and a Freeport office. The mailing address is a post office box in DeFuniak Springs. Branches are open weekdays into late afternoon, with a slightly later Wednesday start.

Questions about the estimated tax on a TRIM notice go to the property appraiser. Payment and delinquency questions go to the collector. The county stretches from the Gulf coast to the inland towns, so a seller may live a long way from the office holding the file. Online payment and the parcel search save the trip.

The collector posts a month-by-month schedule. Here are the entries a home seller will care about.

Walton County real estate tax calendar
MonthWhat is due or happens
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchExemptions due to the Property Appraiser by March 1; full amount due by March 31; fourth installment due March 31
AprilUnpaid real estate tax delinquent April 1 with a 3% charge; installment plan applications for next year due April 30
MayDelinquent real estate taxes advertised once a week for three weeks; certificate sale on or before June 1
June to SeptemberFirst installment due June 30, second due September 30
NovemberBills mailed; 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due December 31

The property appraiser mails the TRIM notice in August.

The plan splits the year into four payments, with a discount on the first three.

  • Applications for the following year are due April 30.
  • The prior year's tax must exceed $100.00 and not be paid through escrow.
  • June 30 brings the first installment with a 6% discount, September 30 the second at 4.5%, December 31 the third at 3%, and March 31 the fourth with no discount.
  • The first two payments are each one quarter of the previous year's taxes.
  • Miss the first payment and the owner is out of the plan for the year.

Enrolled taxpayers do not need to reapply each year. A seller on the plan should ask the collector for the balance left after each payment, since the later installments are adjusted after the roll is set.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go delinquent
sections.html:
Real estate tax still open on April 1 turns delinquent, and the collector adds a 3% charge to the gross figure. Business equipment is treated differently and gathers 1.5% interest each month.

Next, the delinquent list appears in the DeFuniak Herald three weeks running, and an advertising and auction fee lands on your account. The certificate sale follows, scheduled by June 1 as an online auction at lienhub.com/county/walton. Bidding starts at 18% and drops in quarter-percent steps, with a 5% minimum interest unless the bid is zero. A certificate stays alive for seven years.

A holder who has sat on the certificate for two years after the April 1 delinquency date may ask for a tax deed. The Clerk of Court schedules those sales, which run online at walton.realforeclose.com, and you can still redeem right up until the clerk signs the deed. Accepted payment types are cash, cashier's check, money order and card, and cards add a convenience fee.

sections.h2: Exemptions and the March 1 filing date
sections.html:
A homestead exemption belongs to the person, not the house. Once you sell, it ends, and the new owner files separately with the property appraiser by March 1.

Homestead is worth up to $50,000 off taxable value. The first $25,000 reduces every levy, while a second amount reduces only non-school levies on value above $50,000. Renting the home out or moving away forfeits it.

The tax collector also has a page on military property taxes. Servicemembers who rent out a homestead are covered by a separate state provision, so ask the collector whether it applies.

sections.h2: Who pays the taxes when a Walton County home sells?
sections.html:
Your sales contract sets the split. Most Florida deals prorate taxes through the closing date, with the title agent pulling the current balance and any certificate from the collector and charging it to the seller's column.

Deed stamps are collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded, at 70 cents per $100 of the price, and each party on the document can be held liable no matter who agreed to pay. Recording charges start at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, plus a few extra per-page fees.

If the house carries a certificate, redeem it at or before closing. A buyer who spots a certificate more than two years old should ask the Clerk of Court if someone has applied for a tax deed.

Start with a call to the tax collector, since the price of waiting climbs monthly. Closing before April sidesteps the 3% charge and advertising fee. Closing after the certificate sale means interest and extra fees on top.

  • Search the parcel on the tax collector's payment portal for the current balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate exists and what rate it sold at.
  • Check homestead status with the property appraiser before March 1.
  • Tell the title company so the payoff is ordered ahead of the closing date.

A cash buyer can close on a short timeline, but the payoff letter still has to be in hand before the closing date.

Tax on business equipment follows a harsher track than real estate. Unpaid tangible personal property tax is delinquent April 1 and picks up 1.5% interest for each month.

Within 45 days after the March 31 deadline, delinquent accounts are advertised in a local newspaper at the owner's cost. A list is published once in May, and warrant processing begins June 1. A landlord or small business owner selling a rental with equipment inside should ask the collector whether a personal property account sits under the same owner name.

  • Discounts match real estate: 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, 1% in February.
  • Delinquent real estate carries a flat 3% charge, not monthly interest.
  • Different advertising rules apply to each, so ask which list a parcel is on.

sections.h2: What does a certificate holder have to wait for?
sections.html:
The holder cannot move fast. A certificate on a Walton County parcel is valid for seven years, and the holder may apply for a tax deed only two years after the April 1 delinquency date. Under state law the holder also may not contact the owner to demand payment during the first two years.

For the seller, that window is time to arrange a sale. Many owners use it to list the house, find a buyer, and let the closing agent redeem the certificate from proceeds. Ask the collector for the redemption total on the planned closing date, because interest runs by the month.

faqs.q: When do Walton County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Unpaid real estate tax is delinquent on that date and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount.

faqs.q: What is the Walton County installment plan discount?
faqs.a: 6% on the first installment, 4.5% on the second, 3% on the third and none on the fourth. Applications are due April 30.

faqs.q: Where does Walton County hold its tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: Online, at lienhub.com/county/walton, on or before June 1. Bidding starts at 18% and goes down in quarter-percent steps.

faqs.q: Can I still keep my house after a Walton County tax certificate is sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The owner may redeem until the Clerk of Court signs the tax deed. A tax deed application cannot be filed until two years after the April 1 delinquency date.

faqs.q: When is the Walton County exemption deadline?
faqs.a: March 1. Exemptions are due to the Property Appraiser's Office by that date.
